title: Fix SH lightmap coefficients for direct lights

labels.name: cherrypick:4.4
labels.description: Considered for cherry-picking into a future 4.4.x release

body:
Fixes #102300 by unattenuating the directional component (L1), then ensuring that the L0 and L1 components maintain the required ratio for L1 packing to work correctly while preserving consistent energy.

| Dynamic | Non-Directional | Current Directional | PR Directional |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| ![Dynamic](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cf9530d-f5df-4085-9c73-c746bf6b815a) | ![Non-Directionl](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46569492-4b10-4c94-b524-4eb0fa7bd245) | ![Current-Directional](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8215887-5293-4cad-9de5-9c95d182f093) | ![PR-Directional](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24a36705-a04c-4210-9a26-f4e7bba73741) | 
|![SH-Dynamic](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36309021-c759-4bf8-baad-a3c52c7fdfaa) |![SH-Non-Directional](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78a07b1a-5456-4ab0-ab40-fb927c9905ce) |![SH-Current-Directional](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26b363cc-becc-4708-8dc9-080b29a52ae9) |![SH-PR-Directional](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ebabaa1-fdbc-40a3-b673-b8e5e2c365a9) |

Tested using:
[BakedDirectional.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20614944/BakedDirectional.zip)
[sh-lightmaps.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20615099/sh-lightmaps.zip)

For this PR, I assumed directional lightmaps should be indistinguishable from non-directional lightmaps at least for surfaces with normal vectors. 

During sampling, the L0 and L1 components of the lightmap are treated differently. L0 is effectively treated as a constant that gets added to the current light total. L1, on the other hand, is sampled using the surface normal, which is equivalent to a dot product and acts as an attenuation factor. The light value used is already attenuated by a dot product with the surface normal. This results in a double attenuation of the L1 component, causing the light to appear dimmer than intended. Simply undoing this double attenuation makes the light appear too bright, as the L0 component is never attenuated.

Therefore, only the L0 component should remain unattenuated. However, this is easier said than done, since the L1 components are packed using L0, and there exists a defined relationship between the two components (L1 = 4 × L0). This PR addresses the issue by dynamically calculating the L0 and L1 coefficients for direct lights so that all of the above requirements are met. Additionally, the total brightness or energy of the light should be preserved. This results in the following equations:
```
attenuation = dot(normal, light_dir);
Light_L1 = Light_L0 / attenuation; 
4 = (c_L0 * Light_L1) / (c_L1 * Light_L0); // Required ratio imposed by L1 packing
1 = c_L0 + c_L1; // Requirement imposed by "energy" or "brightness"
```

Solving for c_L0 and c_L1 results in the following:
```
c_L0 = 1 / (1 + 4 * attenuation);
c_L1 = 1 - c_L0;
```

These coefficients (c_L0 and c_L1), along with the selected unattenuation of the L1 components, are then applied.

These changes won't affect existing lightmaps. That said, it should be considered whether this PR should instead be added on top of #100640.
